data.title: Ukraine war reaches shores of Bulgarian fishing village
data.description: KRAPETS (BULGARIA) - After a series of drone attacks on ships off the coast, the conflict in Ukraine has taken on a new immediacy for residents of Krapets, a tiny Bulgarian Black Sea fishing village.

data.title: Macron: French protesters ‘exploited’ by political forces
data.description: PARIS - French President Emmanuel Macron believes students waging three weeks of protests that have closed many schools have “legitimate” grievances but are also being “exploited” by political forces, a government spokeswoman said on Wednesday.

data.title: Israeli settlers set fire to mosque in West Bank
data.description: MIKHMAS, Palestinian Territories - Israeli settlers set fire to a mosque and graffitied its outside walls on Wednesday in the occupied West Bank village of Mikhmas, Palestinian sources and the Israeli military said.

data.title: Drone hits data centre of Russia’s largest bank
data.description: MOSCOW - A drone hit a data centre belonging to the Russian state-owned lender Sberbank, a company executive said Wednesday, though the bank’s systems and services were operating normally.

data.title: Pope recovering after lung cancer operation
data.description: ROME - Pope Leo XIV began post-surgery recovery on Wednesday after a tumour removed from his lung was found to be cancerous, plunging the Catholic Church into a period of uncertainty.

data.title: Indonesian haze causes spike in Singapore pollution
data.description: SINGAPORE - Air pollution in parts of Singapore hit the country’s “very high” band on Wednesday while Timor-Leste shut schools, as haze from forest fires raging in Indonesia causes a regional crisis.

data.title: Fuel shortage triggers queues on Bali
data.description: DENPASAR, Indonesia - Moldovan tourist Raisa Neagu spent hours on Wednesday waiting to fuel up her scooter, one of many people snared in a petrol shortage on resort island Bali that authorities blamed on supply disruptions.

data.title: Zelensky accuses Putin of disrespecting Trump
data.description: KYIV - Ukraine on Wednesday accused Russia of wilfully flouting Donald Trump’s purported “energy ceasefire” and passing up an opportunity to ease hostilities, after a renewed wave of deadly strikes across the country that also hit vital power supplies.

data.title: China-North Korea bridge to open 12 years late
data.description: BEIJING - A new bridge linking China and North Korea will finally open on Thursday, 12 years after its construction, with Beijing vowing it will spur trade and “enhance the well-being of the two peoples”.

data.title: Trump touts ‘massive’ oil and mineral exploration in Greenland
data.description: WASHINGTON - US President Donald Trump said Wednesday that oil, gas and mineral exploration was preparing to begin in Greenland, and hailed the Arctic island’s position for US and European security.

data.title: Indian ‘cockroach’ leaders sent to jail after protest
data.description: NEW DELHI - Two leaders of India’s youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) were remanded in custody for five days on Wednesday, as police racheted up efforts to clamp down on anti-election commission protests.

data.title: IMF chief says Saudi attacks could have negative spillover 'everywhere'
data.description: International Monetary Fund head Kristalina Georgieva said Wednesday that recent attacks on Saudi Arabia could impact people "everywhere", as conflict in the energy-rich region adds to wide-ranging economic concerns.

data.title: Ukraine ex-military officer to stand trial over Nord Stream sabotage
data.description: HAMBURG - A former Ukrainian military officer is set to become the first person to stand trial over the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline bombings as proceedings began in a German court Wednesday.

data.title: China heads for record trade surplus as exports surge
data.description: BEIJING - China's exports soared in September, official data showed Wednesday, putting it on course for a record annual trade surplus -- and likely more friction with the European Union and the United States.

data.title: South Korean FA condemns 'personal attacks' as rift rumours grow
data.description: SEOUL - South Korea's football association has told fans to stop "excessive personal attacks", warning of the "psychological burden" it could inflict on national team players in the crosshairs since their World Cup flop.

data.title: Premier League move a Sage decision for new Palace boss
data.description: LONDON - Pierre Sage has admitted the opportunity to manage in the Premier League was one he could simply not refuse as he prepares to return to his native France with Crystal Palace this week.

data.title: Deluge by design: Thai villages flooded to protect capital
data.description: AYUTTHAYA (THAILAND) - Stilt houses in villages north of Bangkok are no longer high enough to stay dry as Thai authorities deliberately flood riverside communities to spare the capital.

data.title: Vietnam mourns 700 war dead in major push to identify missing
data.description: HO CHI MINH CITY - Vietnam held funeral rites for more than 700 of its war dead on Wednesday, unearthed in a major push to identify those missing from decades of conflict with France and the United States.

data.title: Israelis fly from around world to vote in pivotal election
data.description: JERUSALEM - Liran Naaman said he spent 800 euros (nearly US$900) to fly from Amsterdam, where he has lived for the past 11 years, to his native Israel, all to vote in the October 27 election.

data.title: What we know about Pope Leo XIV's lung cancer operation
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - Pope Leo XIV had a cancerous tumour surgically removed from his right lung on Tuesday in a 90-minute operation described as "successful" by the Vatican.

data.title: Ivan Deforge, the French 'bison tamer' in Moscow
data.description: MOSCOW - "Go!" shouted Ivan Deforge, and without hesitation his 300kg hairy sidekicks Karym and Ural leapt through a ring of fire under the dome of the Great Moscow Circus.

data.title: India shuts down iconic Delhi protest site after three decades
data.description: NEW DELHI (INDIA) - For more than three decades, a stretch of road in central New Delhi was where Indians came to be heard, staging rallies to press their demands and hold those in power accountable.

data.title: Japan urges Russia for 'impartial treatment' of arrested journalist
data.description: TOKYO - Tokyo said on Wednesday it had urged Moscow to ensure "fair and impartial treatment" for a Japanese journalist who was arrested by Russia on suspicion of espionage.

data.title: EU takes a page from Ireland's AI playbook
data.description: DUBLIN - The EU wants to catch up in the AI race by taking a cue from Ireland — an early adopter of the technology which has rolled out the red carpet for data centres despite local backlash.

data.title: Saudi employee arrested for allegedly bugging OpenAI office
data.description: SAN FRANCISCO (UNITED STATES) - A Saudi employee of OpenAI was arrested after allegedly planting a recording device in one of the company's San Francisco offices, the AI firm and federal prosecutors said Tuesday.

data.title: Global deforestation slowed in 2025 but surged in Congo basin: study
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - Deforestation slowed worldwide last year, but the improvement is unlikely to last as the situation deteriorates in Central Africa and an exceptionally strong El Nino weather pattern intensifies, a new study said on Wednesday.

data.title: Microsoft's Brad Smith calls for 'real and effective' AI safety standards
data.description: DUBLIN - Microsoft president Brad Smith warned Tuesday that industry and governments must "act with urgency" to create "real and effective safety standards" to contain the risks linked to artificial intelligence.

data.title: US fines Bank of America $1.2 bn for anti-money laundering violations
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - The US Treasury Department said Tuesday that it is imposing penalties of more than $1.2 billion on Bank of America, citing "violations of anti-money laundering and sanctions laws."

data.title: Trump, White House post video of UK man killed by tiger
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - US President Donald Trump posted disturbing footage on his Truth Social account Tuesday of a man being fatally mauled by a tiger in Britain, sparking backlash on social media.

data.title: Bipartisan US senators urge Trump to scrap Russian diesel deal
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - Republican and Democratic US senators joined forces Tuesday to urge President Donald Trump to scrap his diesel deal with Russia, calling it a "betrayal" that would bankroll Moscow's war in Ukraine while doing little to ease soaring fuel prices.

data.title: Cornell suspends frat parties after alleged gang rape
data.description: NEW YORK - Cornell University on Tuesday suspended fraternities' parties and social events for the remaining academic year following outcry over an alleged gang rape at one of the elite college's all-male clubs.

data.title: Ex-gang leader sentenced to minimum 40 years for Tupac murder
data.description: LOS ANGELES (UNITED STATES) - Duane "Keffe D" Davis, the former Los Angeles gang leader who boasted for years of his involvement in the killing of rapper Tupac Shakur, only to deny it when he came to trial, was sentenced to a minimum 40 years in prison on Tuesday.

data.title: No lights, no friends: Cuban youth grapple with loneliness
data.description: HAVANA - With frequent power cuts transforming Havana into a ghost town, young Cubans are struggling to get their kicks, many resorting to games of dominoes with strangers to pass the time.

data.title: Pope Leo admitted to hospital for lung surgery
data.description: VATICAN CITY - Pope Leo XIV was admitted to hospital in Rome on Tuesday for surgery to remove a nodule on his lung, but cardinals said he appeared "very relaxed" about the operation.

data.title: AI could 'change the stakes' on bioweapons: UK spy chief
data.description: LONDON - The head of Britain's domestic spy agency warned Tuesday that artificial intelligence was affecting the security risks faced by the UK, and could "change the stakes" on bioweapons.
